statement_resolution.source_wording: 自动定理证明的方法 (a method of automated theorem proving)
statement_resolution.reason: The repository metadata names Robinson's resolution method but gives no proposition. It does not choose propositional versus first-order clauses, ground versus lifted resolution, factoring, clause semantics, a derivability relation, or whether the intended result is local soundness, refutation completeness, or a lifting theorem. These choices yield distinct theorems.
statement_resolution.required_resolution: A source owner must select a proposition-level theorem from a pinpoint edition of Robinson's paper (or another primary source) and freeze its clause syntax, semantics, inference rules, equality policy, and all finiteness or satisfiability hypotheses.

primary_source_candidate.citation: J. A. Robinson, A Machine-Oriented Logic Based on the Resolution Principle, Journal of the ACM 12(1), 1965, 23-41
primary_source_candidate.credit: discovery anchor only; theorem/page premises and errata have not been audited

candidate_scopes_not_adopted.name: binary resolution soundness
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.shape: Every resolvent is a logical consequence of its two parent clauses.
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.exclusion_reason: This is a local inference-rule theorem and does not by itself express resolution's refutation completeness.

candidate_scopes_not_adopted.name: propositional resolution refutation completeness
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.shape: An unsatisfiable finite propositional clause set derives the empty clause by resolution.
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.exclusion_reason: The repository source does not restrict the method to propositional logic or fix finiteness and derivation conventions.

candidate_scopes_not_adopted.name: first-order resolution refutation completeness
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.shape: An unsatisfiable first-order clause set has a resolution refutation, with a specified lifted rule and any required factoring.
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.exclusion_reason: Several formulations differ in clause representation, standardizing apart, unification, factoring, equality, and compactness assumptions; none is selected by the metadata.

candidate_scopes_not_adopted.name: resolution lifting lemma
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.shape: A ground resolution step or refutation lifts to a first-order resolution derivation.
candidate_scopes_not_adopted.exclusion_reason: This is an important component of completeness, but the source record does not identify it as the root theorem.
